# Ref Commons Playbook

When I see the sustainable share calculation, I will use it as my baseline target for each season, not as a ceiling to exceed.

When I observe other boats catching consistently above the sustainable share, I will recognize this as a signal that defection is occurring and adjust my strategy accordingly rather than continuing pure cooperation.

When the stock is declining season-to-season, I will treat this as evidence that collective overfishing is happening and that my cooperative catches alone cannot save the fishery.

When I'm ahead of the sustainable pace partway through the game, I will not use this as justification to catch above the sustainable share going forward—past success doesn't give me permission to deplete future stock.

When it's not the final season, I will prioritize stock preservation by catching at or slightly below the sustainable share, since future seasons depend on it.

When it is the final season, I will still catch approximately the sustainable share rather than maximize in that round, since I've committed to a preservation strategy throughout and abandoning it at the end is inconsistent.

When reasoning about my catch level, I will actually compare my total catch against the cumulative sustainable total (sustainable share × seasons elapsed), not just my recent decisions.

I will not rationalize above-sustainable catches by framing them as "competitive" or "slightly above"—the sustainable share is the target, and I should hit it or stay below it consistently.

When I submit a catch amount, I will verify it matches my stated reasoning before finalizing it.

# Playbook for ref_commons

When I see the sustainable catch level, I will use it as my baseline target, not as a ceiling to exceed.

When the stock is healthy and I'm early in the game, I will catch at or very slightly below the sustainable share. Restraint early preserves the resource for later seasons where I can still benefit.

When I'm tempted to exceed the sustainable catch, I will remember that each boat overfishing compounds—if I take 13 and others take 13, the stock collapses faster than if we all take 10.7. My gain from one extra fish is negated by the system-wide damage.

When I find myself already above my cumulative fair share, I will not use that as justification to catch more. Instead, I will return to the sustainable level to signal cooperation and stabilize the stock.

When a season is the last one, I will not abandon my strategy. The final season is not an excuse to overfish—others will think the same way and we'll all suffer. I will stick to sustainable catches throughout.

When I see the stock declining across seasons (100 → 97.5 → 96.0 → 94.9 → 92.6 → 93.0), I will recognize this as a warning that the fishery is being overstressed, not a signal to catch more while I can.

I will catch consistently at the sustainable share level across all seasons. The game rewards total fish landed over six seasons, and the sustainable strategy keeps the stock healthy enough to produce that total. Overfishing in early seasons to reach 69 total is not optimal—a disciplined approach across all seasons would yield more.

When I submit my catch, I will match it to the sustainable share shown to me that season, within ±0.5 tolerance for small variations.

# Playbook for ref_commons

**On my opening move:** Start at or slightly below the sustainable share. This establishes cooperative intent and gives me data on what other boats do.

**On detecting others' behavior:** Watch what other boats catch in early seasons. If they consistently exceed the sustainable share, abandon the assumption that cooperation will emerge.

**On my competitive position:** Track my cumulative catch against the sustainable total I could have accumulated. When I fall behind, I need to catch more per season to stay competitive—but calibrate this carefully against stock depletion.

**On stock monitoring:** Check the stock level each season against the previous season. A declining trend means I'm in a race against depletion, not a leisurely harvest. Adjust upward faster when stock drops.

**On mid-game strategy:** Once I'm into seasons 3-4, I should have enough data to know whether restraint is being reciprocated. If other boats are taking 11-13 while the sustainable share is 10-11, match their behavior or exceed it slightly to avoid falling too far behind.

**On the final season:** The last season has no future penalty. I can take what I need to hit a competitive total, but by then the sustainable share ceiling should still guide me—taking significantly more invites the tragedy of the commons to fully manifest and wastes the opportunity to end with a healthy stock.

**What did not work:** My early-game restraint in season 2 (catching 9.5) cost me competitiveness and didn't encourage reciprocal restraint from others. Defection by others will happen regardless of my virtue signaling.

**My actual edge:** I should catch closer to what others are catching, not what is sustainable in isolation. The sustainable share is a ceiling, but other boats' actual behavior is my real constraint.
